claims.note: Tempelhofer Feld has been open for public recreation since 2010, with more than 300 hectares available for leisure activities and nature.
The site supports protected plants and rare animal species, as well as recreation and civic initiatives.

claims.source_section: An urban open space with a multi-layered history
claims.note: The site's recorded history includes aviation, Nazi-era persecution and forced labour, and the Berlin Airlift of 1948–49.

claims.source_section: An urban open space with a multi-layered history
claims.note: Airport operations ceased in 2008; the former airfield opened to the public in 2010.

claims.source_section: An urban open space with a multi-layered history
claims.note: The official overview describes the 2014 vote as rejecting development at the edges and supporting preservation of the field, followed by a preservation law in June 2014.
The Law for the Preservation of Tempelhofer Feld (ThFG) came into force in June 2014 following the referendum.
Citizens, the relevant Senate administration and Grün Berlin jointly developed the development and maintenance plan (EPP) during 2014–2016.
The EPP took effect in May 2016 and addresses nature, history, recreation and civic engagement.
A continuing participation model involves administration, Grün Berlin and elected citizens in implementing measures for the field.
The Senate describes an international ideas competition and public dialogue aimed at informing debate, explicitly distinguishing this process from a decision to build on the field's perimeter.
The Senate frames the dialogue in relation to housing demand, social infrastructure, climate change and transport transition.

claims.source_section: Dialogprozess Tempelhofer Feld; Fragen und Antworten
claims.note: The process includes dialogue workshops involving Berlin residents selected by random sampling and an international ideas competition, and is presented as a contribution to broader public debate.
